query: Consider the following context: Conventional material processing approaches often achieve strengthening of materials at the cost of reduced ductility. In that context, which method can be used for overcome the strength-ductility trade-off, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Engineering coherent internal boundaries at the nanoscale can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in materials.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional materials with reduced ductility due to strengthening.
generation.intervention: Introduction of coherent internal boundaries at the nanoscale.
generation.mechanism: Dislocation dissociation and gliding in conjugate slip systems.
generation.uncertainty: Effectiveness of nanoscale engineering in various material systems.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of materials with engineered nanoscale internal boundaries.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the material with engineered nanoscale internal boundaries does not exhibit enhanced strength and ductility compared to the conventional material, the hypothesis is falsified.

Own digest: Paper card. Question: Can a novel hybrid-rolling process combining cryo-rolling and warm-rolling create a dual structural-compositional heterogeneous microstructure in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy to achieve unprecedented strength-ductility synergy?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA). Processing: Hybrid-rolling consisting of two stages: Stage I cryo-rolling to a true strain of ~1.2 (90% reduction in thickness total) with samples immersed in liquid N2 for 30 minutes before and after each pass; Stage II warm-rolling at 600 °C to a true strain of ~1.2, with specimens held at 600 °C for 20 minutes prior to each of the ten passes and water quenched immediately after every pass.. Test conditions: Tensile tests performed along the rolling direction (RD) at ambient temperature using a universal testing machine with an initial strain rate of 8.3 × 10−4 s−1..
